chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Benny Goodman's swinging band and quartet
summary: Crawford calls Goodman's band the closest to swing in any white band and lists the quartet.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: And you liked Benny Goodman. What did you like about Goodman's band?
Well, Goodman, Goodman was a natural swinger. That was the closest thing to swinging that I ever heard in any white band, oh, yes. Goodman was a swinger, swinging band. Listen --
You said it was the closest thing you ever heard to swinging in a white band. --
And even in his quartet, when he had Lionel Hampton. I should mention Goodman on clarinet, but Goodman on clarinet, Lionel Hampton on vibes, Teddy Wilson on bass, Sid Bernstein on --
No, Sid Bernstein on bass and Teddy Wilson on piano.
There was a lady that called up here and --
Oh, it's Artie Bernstein on bass. Sid or Artie?
